chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Sulayman ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari, who said:

I saw Aba al-Hasan عليه السلام wake from his sleep, perform wudu (ablution), and not perform istinja'. And he عليه السلام said, as if expressing amazement at a man whom he named: "It has reached me that when wind comes out from him, he performs istinja'."
As for that which indicates the obligation of istinja' upon one who defecates.

key_terms.الِاسْتِنْجَاءِ: istinja'; ritual cleaning after relieving oneself
key_terms.يَسْتَنْجِي: he performs istinja', cleansing the private area after excretion

ai.seo_question: Does passing wind require istinja' in Shia fiqh, or only wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that Imam Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام would perform wudu (ablution) after sleep without performing istinja', and he expressed amazement at someone who would perform istinja' merely due to passing wind. The text indicates a legal distinction between what necessitates wudu (ablution) and what necessitates istinja', while introducing evidence concerning the obligation of istinja' for one who has defecated.
